method.sampling: The app's hourly series (the ephemeris table's rows at the top of each hour) against the same sky every minute from SPICE (DE440, MOON_ME, LT+S from the Moon's centre, as the table was made) with the same skyline, Sun disk test and battery walk. An event's sampling error is its hourly time (the first hourly sample in the new state) minus the one-minute crossing, refined linearly between minutes; battery times are to the minute.
method.terrain: Skylines traced through PGDA product 90's adjusted models (20 m within 6 km south of 87.55° S, 80 m to 100 km, 240 m to 220 km, the app's bands, march and 2 m mast), and the same skylines raised and lowered by one stated height error (the ERR maps, at the point that makes the skyline and at the site, over its distance). An event's terrain spread is the largest shift of its one-minute time under those three skylines; an event that one of them loses is counted apart.
method.ephemeris: The largest gap to JPL Horizons in height plus direction, for each body, divided by the rate of the body's height above the skyline at each one-minute crossing.
method.combination: The supported plus-or-minus is the sum of the three 95th percentiles of the size of each error over the span: sampling, terrain (or, on a flat horizon, a stated allowance) and ephemeris. They are added rather than root-summed because the sampling error is one-sided and the terrain spread is not symmetric. The app shows it rounded up to the next half hour.
method.not_covered: Not in the budget: the lander's own height and tilt, hills smaller than the models resolve, the skyline between its 720 directions, the battery's temperature and age, and anything about the lander keeping warm or starting again after the night.
